item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural.

item.tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

answer_sheet.Enhancement style: Natural-looking blur reduction and sharpening, not a stylised remake.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and framing.
answer_sheet.Subject and background: Keep the same dog, pose, expression, and background.

must_haves: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
The background and full original framing are preserved.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: can you fix this pic of my dog
turns.agent:
I couldn't fix the photo. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was made and no credits were spent.

I tried two ways:
1. **Upscale (2x, "balanced" mode):** This sharpens and adds detail while making the photo bigger. It was turned down for lack of credits.
2. **AI edit to remove the blur (flux-2-klein at 640px):** This is the cheapest option on the free plan, from about 5 credits. It was turned down too, so the balance is probably close to zero.

**To go ahead:**
- **Add credits** by buying a credit pack or upgrading your plan, or wait for your free credits to refill. Then tell me and I'll run it again. I'd use the 2x upscale for the best quality, or the AI edit if you want to spend as little as possible. Keep in mind the AI edit makes a smaller picture (640px on the long side), and it redraws the detail, so small features of your dog could come out slightly different.
- **Or send a sharper copy** if you have one, like another photo from the same moment or the original full-size file. Even a slightly clearer starting photo gives much better results.
